$schema: Datum family app summary, read by the Datum hub site (github.com/Edgar-Mendonca/Datum) and by Help › Roadmap in the app.
name: Datum Atlas
tagline: Choose the right material: property charts, selection and referenced data, in one app for Windows.
for: Design and materials engineers, and students.
about: Datum Atlas helps you pick a material and show why it is the right one. Choose a design goal, such as a light, stiff beam or a cheap, strong tie, and Atlas sets the property chart, the selection line and the limits for you.

Every material is a bubble spanning its range of values, grouped by family. Limits, index lines, bands, boxes, drawn shapes and whole families left out narrow the field; the materials that pass are ranked, and every one that fails says why. Compare the best side by side, add up their energy and CO₂ through a product's life, find the processes that can make the part and what it costs, and print a report. Every value names its source, and you can add, import and share your own materials.

steps.title: Pick a goal
steps.text: Choose a design goal, or set the two properties to chart yourself.

steps.title: Chart and select
steps.text: Move the selection line, add limits and boxes, and watch the field narrow.

steps.title: Rank, check and report
steps.text: See the materials that pass, ranked. Compare the best, audit their energy and CO₂, choose how to make the part, and print the selection report.

highlights: About 250 materials from every family, compiled from open and public sources. Every value names its source; 73 values are checked against published datasheets so far, and gaps stay gaps, never zero.
Property charts of any two properties or of your own formulas, with family envelopes, the best materials labelled and labels kept apart; bar charts; up to four charts side by side.

25 design goals and a library of 52 performance indices, including low-carbon and low-energy ones, with an index builder; a goal sets the axes, the selection line and the limits in one pick, and explains why.
Selection by limits, index lines, bands, boxes, drawn shapes and families; results ranked by an index or by weighted properties, with the reason every other material fails.

An eco audit: energy and CO₂ of a product from its materials to the end of its life, for up to four design options, with the largest phase named, the break-even life, and greener substitutes for the same job.
Process selection from 55 processes: the ones that can make your part from your material, why the others cannot, and the cost per part against batch size; joins and finishes that suit it.

Compare up to six materials with a radar chart, and print a selection report with the charts, shortlist, eco audit, manufacture and datasheets. Your own materials and databases, spreadsheet and CSV import and export, SI or imperial units.

roadmap.title: Assistants
items: A command line and an assistant connection (Model Context Protocol) to search materials, run a selection, the eco audit and process selection.

roadmap.title: Polish
items: A user guide, colour-blind safe colours, imperial units on the eco and process pages, and .ods export.
Processes matched by alloy type, so cast and wrought alloys are told apart.

roadmap.title: Trusted data
items: About 500 materials with specific grades, many more values checked against published datasheets, and search by equivalent designations.
Sandwich panels and lattices, and flags for restricted and critical substances.

roadmap.title: Stable
items: About 1,000 materials, with pictures and microstructures.
A user guide and a signed installer.
